A thigh lift removes excess skin and fat from the inner or outer thighs and tightens the tissue underneath – often after major weight loss or with age – for smoother, firmer contours. MedLuxLife arranges your online consultation with the surgeon in Istanbul and organises your stay.

Quick facts

Anaesthesia

General anaesthesia

Hospital stay

Walking

Within hours

Compression garment

In the first weeks

Stay in Türkiye

Planned individually with the clinic

General information; your surgeon plans the details for you personally.

Who it may be suitable for

  • You have loose skin and excess fat on your thighs, for example after major weight loss or with age.
  • Your weight has been stable for some time.
  • You are in good general health.

Whether the procedure is suitable for you is decided by the surgeon after a personal assessment.

Options

Inner thigh lift

Incisions along the inner thighs for loose skin on the inside of the legs.

Outer thigh lift

Incisions along the outer thighs to tighten the outer contour.

How the operation is performed

Consultation before surgery

The surgeon assesses the areas of concern, discusses your wishes and makes a personal surgical plan.

Anaesthesia and preparation

You receive general anaesthesia. The area is marked to guide the incisions.

Removing excess skin and fat

Incisions are made along the inner or outer thighs; excess skin and fat are removed and the tissue underneath is tightened.

Closure and recovery

The incisions are closed with sutures and compression garments are put on. You usually stay in hospital for 1–2 nights.

Zirconium veneers and crowns are custom-made, metal-free restorations in zirconia ceramic. They cover discolouration, chips or gaps and improve the shape and colour of your teeth with a natural, light-transmitting look. MedLuxLife arranges your online consultation with the dentist in Istanbul and organises your stay.

Quick facts

Anaesthesia

Local anaesthesia

Time in Türkiye

Usually 5–7 days

Material

Metal-free zirconia

Sensitivity

Possible for a few days

Daily life

Right after the treatment

General information; your dentist plans the details for you personally.

Who it may be suitable for

  • Your teeth are stained, chipped, slightly misaligned or have gaps.
  • You would like a durable, natural-looking solution – also suitable if you have a metal allergy.
  • Your gums are healthy and there is enough enamel for veneers.

Whether the treatment is suitable for you is decided by the dentist after a personal assessment.

How the treatment works

Consultation and planning

The dentist assesses your teeth and plans the treatment – often with digital images that show the planned result.

Tooth preparation

A thin layer of enamel is removed under local anaesthesia and precise digital impressions are taken.

Veneer fabrication

The veneers are made in a dental laboratory to match the shape, colour and size you planned.

Bonding and final adjustments

After a trial fitting, the veneers are bonded and fine-tuned for comfort and a natural look.

Whitening gel

Monitoring and sessions

Aftercare

Avoid colouring food and drinks for 48 hours; touch-up kits help to keep the result.

All-on-4 and All-on-6 replace a complete row of teeth in the upper or lower jaw with a fixed bridge on four or six titanium implants – a fixed alternative to removable dentures. With six implants, the biting forces are spread more evenly. MedLuxLife arranges your online consultation with the dentist in Istanbul and organises your stay.

Quick facts

Anaesthesia

Local anaesthesia or sedation

Trips to Türkiye

Usually 2

1st visit

About 3–5 days

Healing time

3–6 months

2nd visit

About 5–7 days

General information; your dentist plans the details for you personally.

Who it may be suitable for

  • You are missing most or all of your teeth in one or both jaws, or your teeth are badly damaged.
  • You wear dentures and would like a fixed solution.
  • You are in good general health; if there is little jawbone, bone grafting can be considered.

Whether the treatment is suitable for you is decided by the dentist after a personal assessment.

Options

All-on-4

A full arch on four angled implants – makes the most of the available bone and often avoids bone grafting.

All-on-6

A full arch on six implants – more stability and an even distribution of the biting forces.

How the treatment works

Preparation and anaesthesia

The dentist examines your teeth and jaw and plans the treatment. The implants are placed under local anaesthesia or sedation.

Implant placement

Four or six titanium implants are placed into the jawbone at specific angles for maximum support.

Temporary teeth

On the same visit a temporary fixed bridge is attached, so you are not left without teeth.

Permanent bridge

After 3–6 months of healing, the permanent bridge is fitted on your second visit.

A dental implant is a fixed replacement for a missing tooth: a titanium post is placed in the jawbone as an artificial root and, once it has grown into the bone, a custom-made crown is attached. Implants restore chewing function and help to preserve the jawbone. MedLuxLife arranges your online consultation with the dentist in Istanbul and organises your stay.

Local anaesthesia

Trips to Türkiye

Usually 2

1st visit

Healing time

2nd visit

General information; your dentist plans the details for you personally.

Who it may be suitable for

  • You are missing one or more teeth and would like a fixed replacement.
  • Your gums are healthy and there is enough jawbone – if not, bone grafting or a sinus lift can help.
  • You are in good general health and ready to keep up good oral hygiene.

Whether the treatment is suitable for you is decided by the dentist after a personal assessment.

Options

Single implant

Replaces one tooth with an implant and a crown.

Several implants

Implant-supported crowns or bridges replace several teeth.

Bone grafting or sinus lift

Builds up the bone if there is not enough for an implant.

How the treatment works

Preparation and anaesthesia

The dentist discusses your wishes and examines your teeth and jaw. The implant is placed under local anaesthesia.

Implant placement

A titanium post is placed precisely into the jawbone as an artificial tooth root.

Healing (osseointegration)

Over the next 3–6 months, the implant grows firmly into the jawbone – you return home in the meantime.

Crown placement

On your second visit, the custom-made crown is attached to the implant.

  • You would like a fuller, more defined eyebrow shape.

Follicle extraction

Single fine follicles are taken from the donor area at the back of the head.

Implantation and shaping

The follicles are implanted with the DHI technique, following the natural growth pattern for an even, symmetrical shape.

Closure and recovery

You are monitored briefly and receive personal aftercare instructions.

For cheeks, jawline and chin – density and design are planned with you.

Preparation and anaesthesia

Follicles are taken from the donor area at the back of the head with the FUE or DHI technique.

Implantation and design

The follicles are implanted into the beard or moustache area in the natural direction of growth; density and shape are planned with you.

Closure and recovery

The donor area is cared for and you receive detailed aftercare instructions.

DHI (Direct Hair Implantation) is a further development of FUE: the follicles are taken individually and implanted directly with a special implanter pen (Choi pen), without opening channels in advance. This gives precise control over the depth, angle and direction of each hair – and DHI is also possible without shaving the head. MedLuxLife arranges your online consultation with the surgeon in Istanbul and organises your stay.

Local anaesthesia

After about 12 months

  • You have thinning hair, a receding hairline or bald patches.
  • You have enough healthy donor hair.
  • You would like to keep your hair long – DHI is also possible without shaving.
  • You are in good general health.

Whether the procedure is suitable for you is decided by the surgeon after a personal assessment.

Options

Classic DHI

Follicles are implanted directly with the Choi pen for a dense, natural hairline.

Unshaven DHI

The recipient area does not have to be shaved – practical for women and for long hair.

How the procedure works

Preparation and anaesthesia

The surgeon discusses your wishes and examines your scalp. On the day of the procedure you receive local anaesthesia.

Follicle extraction

Individual follicles are taken from the donor area at the back or sides of the head.

Direct implantation

The follicles are loaded into the Choi pen and placed directly into the recipient area, with precise control of depth, angle and direction.

Closure and recovery

DHI needs no stitches. You are monitored briefly and receive personal aftercare instructions.

In an FUE hair transplant, individual hair follicles are taken one by one from the donor area – usually the back or sides of the head – with a fine micro-punch and implanted into thinning or bald areas. No linear incision and no stitches are needed. MedLuxLife arranges your online consultation with the surgeon in Istanbul and organises your stay.

Quick facts

Anaesthesia

Local anaesthesia

Duration

About 6–8 hours

Back to work

After about 2–3 days

Final result

After 12–18 months

Stay in Türkiye

Planned individually with the clinic

General information; your surgeon plans the details for you personally.

Who it may be suitable for

  • You have male pattern baldness, thinning hair or a receding hairline.
  • You have enough healthy donor hair at the back or sides of the head.
  • Your hair loss has stabilised.
  • You are in good general health.

Whether the procedure is suitable for you is decided by the surgeon after a personal assessment.

How the procedure works

Preparation and anaesthesia

The surgeon discusses your wishes, examines your hair and scalp and plans the hairline. Local anaesthesia is applied on the day of the procedure.

Follicle extraction

With fine micro-punches, individual follicles are taken from the donor area at the back or sides of the head, where hair is most resistant to hair loss.

Implantation

Medical microbiology provides the laboratory testing behind the diagnosis and treatment of infections. The laboratories at our partner hospital support inpatient, outpatient and emergency care across bacteriology, virology, parasitology, mycology, molecular microbiology and infection immunology, with a broad and regularly updated test panel. MedLuxLife coordinates sample collection during your visit and ensures your results are translated and shared with your doctors.

Treatments and services

Bacteriology

Identification of bacteria and antibiotic susceptibility testing, combining classical culture with rapid confirmatory methods and same-day stained microscopy.

Mycobacteriology (tuberculosis)

Isolation and identification of acid-fast organisms such as Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Mycobacterium avium complex, including molecular methods and the Quantiferon TB Gold test.

Virology

Antigen and antibody serology, sensitive detection of HIV and hepatitis agents, and confirmatory testing where needed.

Parasitology

Diagnosis of parasitic infections using classical methods supported by serological tests.

Mycology

Identification of yeasts, dermatophytes and moulds, plus galactomannan antigen testing for suspected aspergillus infection in immunocompromised patients.

Molecular microbiology

PCR-based detection, genotyping and viral load testing, including viruses monitored after transplantation.

Syndromic molecular panels

Rapid multiplex testing of blood cultures, respiratory, gastrointestinal, cerebrospinal and joint fluid samples, with simultaneous detection of resistance genes.

Infection immunology

Immunological tests that support the diagnosis of infectious diseases.

Round-the-clock service

The laboratory operates 24 hours a day and works closely with clinicians on diagnosis and treatment.

Selected tests

  • Bacterial culture and antibiotic susceptibility testing
  • Stained microscopy of clinical samples
  • Acid-fast bacteria staining
  • Quantiferon TB Gold
  • Galactomannan antigen test
  • Hepatitis B virus DNA
  • Hepatitis C virus RNA
  • Varicella zoster virus (VZV)
  • Epstein-Barr virus (EBV DNA)
  • Cytomegalovirus (CMV DNA)
  • Polyomavirus (BK/JC virus)
  • Human papillomavirus (HPV DNA) and genotyping
  • Viral load tests
  • MRSA (real-time PCR)
  • VRE (real-time PCR)
  • Neisseria gonorrhoeae (real-time PCR)
  • Chlamydia (real-time PCR)
  • Syndromic panels for blood culture, respiratory, gastrointestinal, CSF and joint fluid samples
  • Resistance gene detection

Cytopathology

On-site sample adequacy assessment

Medical genetics diagnoses inherited and non-inherited conditions caused by changes in genes, and helps individuals and families understand their risks, including carrier status and risks for future children. The genetic diagnosis centre at our partner hospital offers genetic consultations and counselling alongside cytogenetic, molecular cytogenetic and molecular genetic testing in ISO 15189 accredited laboratories. MedLuxLife coordinates your appointments and the practical steps of your visit.

Treatments and services

Genetic consultation

Outpatient examination by a medical geneticist to assess whether a genetic condition may be present.

Genetic counselling

Explanation of results, risk assessment for relatives and future generations, and planning of preventive options, also for families referred from other centres.

Prenatal genetic diagnosis

Testing during pregnancy when screening suggests increased risk, with advanced maternal age, or when a parent carries a known genetic condition.

Postnatal genetic diagnosis

Testing in children and adults when a genetic cause is suspected, including recurrent miscarriage, infertility and hereditary neurological or muscle diseases.

Cytogenetics

Karyotype analysis on blood, amniotic fluid, chorionic villus, fetal blood and bone marrow samples.

Molecular cytogenetics

FISH testing, including rapid detection of common chromosomal changes and microdeletion syndromes, and molecular karyotyping (array CGH).

Molecular genetic testing

DNA analyses for single-gene diseases and carrier status.

Oncology and haematology genetics

FISH and DNA analyses on tumour tissue and bone marrow, used as markers for disease course and possible response to chemotherapy.

Interdisciplinary cooperation

Close collaboration with paediatrics, obstetrics and gynaecology, internal medicine, neurology, neurosurgery and pathology.

Situations in which genetic testing may be considered

  • Increased risk of a chromosomal anomaly in pregnancy screening
  • Advanced maternal age
  • Known carrier status for a chromosomal or single-gene disease
  • Down syndrome (trisomy 21) and other common chromosomal anomalies - rapid FISH on amniocentesis samples
  • Rapid chromosomal analysis on chorionic villus biopsy samples
  • Karyotype and DNA analyses on fetal blood samples
  • Congenital anomalies
  • Growth, developmental and intellectual disabilities
  • Short stature
  • Global developmental delay
  • Recurrent miscarriage
  • Infertility
  • Single-gene diseases more common in consanguineous families
  • Hereditary neurological and muscle diseases appearing in adulthood
  • Suspected inherited predisposition to thrombosis
  • Oncology and haematology patients (tumour tissue and bone marrow analyses)

Medical imaging underpins the diagnosis and treatment planning of many conditions. The imaging unit at our partner hospital brings together radiology and nuclear medicine specialists with a broad range of modern equipment and fully digital reporting. MedLuxLife schedules your examinations and shares preparation instructions in advance; the hospital provides your images and reports for you and your doctors at home.

Treatments and services

MRI and functional MRI

3 Tesla MRI, including functional MRI to map vital brain areas before tumour surgery, and MR proton and phosphorus spectroscopy to characterise tumours.

PET/CT

Shows the metabolic activity of tumours and helps determine their location, and can be used to monitor response to treatment.

Nuclear medicine and SPECT

Gamma camera and SPECT imaging, reported by nuclear medicine specialists.

CT, X-ray and fluoroscopy

Multi-slice CT, digital direct radiography, digital fluoroscopy, portable X-ray and C-arm imaging.

Breast and bone imaging

Digital mammography and bone densitometry for breast assessment and bone health.

Ultrasound

4D ultrasonography and Doppler ultrasonography for organ and blood flow assessment.

Molecular imaging

Techniques that add functional and metabolic information to anatomical images, which may help classify tumours and in some cases reduce the need for biopsy.

Interventional radiology

Minimally invasive, image-guided treatments carried out in the dedicated interventional radiology unit, using flat panel digital angiography (DSA).

Digital archiving (PACS and RIS)

All images and reports are stored digitally, shared across the hospital and can be exchanged with imaging centres abroad.

Research

A university setting with ongoing research, including the development of a molecular imaging research unit.

Preparation forms

Before your examination you may be asked to complete a patient information form, an MRI preparation form and a pregnancy information and consent form for radiological examinations.

The department at our partner hospital offers a wide range of diagnostic and therapeutic endoscopy, alongside dedicated care for reflux, liver disease, inflammatory bowel disease and colorectal cancer screening. Treatments and services

Diagnostic endoscopy

Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, colonoscopy and double-balloon endoscopy (enteroscopy), which can examine parts of the small intestine beyond the reach of standard scopes, for example in unexplained bleeding, iron-deficiency anaemia or suspected Crohn's disease.

Endoscopic treatment of bleeding

Band ligation, sclerotherapy, haemoclips and argon laser treatment for bleeding from the stomach or intestines.

Treatment of narrowing

Balloon dilatation and stent placement for strictures of the stomach or intestines.

Endoscopic obesity treatment

Intragastric balloon placement during upper endoscopy, which may support weight loss alongside lifestyle changes; the balloon is removed after a set period.

Upper endoscopy, 24-hour pH monitoring and motility studies, followed by medication, endoscopic options such as the Stretta procedure and endoscopic fundoplication (for example Plicator or Gastrofix), or surgery.

Urea breath test and stool antigen testing to diagnose H. pylori infection and guide treatment.

Screening colonoscopy with polypectomy, as polyps can be found and removed during the procedure; people at higher risk receive an individual screening plan.

ERCP

Endoscopic imaging of the bile and pancreatic ducts, which also allows stone removal, stent placement to relieve blockages and biopsy.

Haemorrhoid treatment

Medication for early stages and band ligation, sclerotherapy, laser or infrared treatment during sedated colonoscopy for intermediate stages, with referral for surgery in advanced cases.

Hepatology unit

Diagnosis and long-term follow-up of chronic hepatitis B and C using liver function tests, HBV and HCV PCR, abdominal ultrasound and liver biopsy, with antiviral treatment options including interferon.

Diagnosis of ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease by colonoscopy and/or double-balloon enteroscopy, and ongoing medical treatment.

Audiology covers the detailed assessment and rehabilitation of hearing and balance problems in babies, children and adults. The department at our partner hospital offers a broad range of hearing and vestibular tests, including objective tests suitable for infants and for people with dizziness. MedLuxLife helps families schedule tests at suitable times, explains preparation requirements in advance and arranges for results to be shared with your doctors at home.

Treatments and services

Newborn hearing screening

Screening of babies' hearing using BERA so that possible hearing loss can be identified early.

Clinical BERA (ABR)

An objective electrophysiological test that measures the auditory nerve's response to sound through electrodes placed on the head, used especially for infants who did not pass screening, babies with risk factors and children with speech delay who cannot complete other tests. It is also known as ABR, BAEP or BAER.

Clinical otoacoustic emissions and ASSR

TEOAE/DPOAE and auditory steady-state response testing, which can support and complement BERA findings.

Child audiometry

Age-appropriate hearing tests including behavioural observation audiometry, visual reinforcement audiometry and play audiometry, as well as free field testing.

Adult hearing evaluation

Pure-tone and speech audiometry, plus high-frequency audiometry where indicated.

Middle ear and Eustachian tube tests

Tympanometry and acoustic reflex testing, high-frequency (1000 Hz) tympanometry for babies up to six months, and Eustachian tube function testing.

Videonystagmography (VNG)

Records eye movements with video goggles during oculomotor, positional and caloric tests to help determine whether dizziness originates in the inner ear or the brain.

Video head impulse test (vHIT)

Assesses the vestibulo-ocular reflex of each semicircular canal separately.

VEMP test

Vestibular evoked myogenic potentials, used in the differential diagnosis of conditions such as semicircular canal dehiscence, early Meniere's disease and otolith organ dysfunction.

Caloric and rotational testing

Caloric vestibular testing (ENG) and rotational examination to evaluate the function of each balance organ and central compensation.

Repositioning manoeuvres for BPPV

When benign paroxysmal positional vertigo is identified, corrective manoeuvres such as Epley, Vannucchi, Gufoni and BBQ roll may be performed.

Preparing a child for BERA

The test is usually done during natural sleep without medication, so babies are brought awake and fasted for feeding and sleep at the clinic; evening appointments, or testing under general anaesthesia with an anaesthetist at the family's request, may be arranged.

  • Speech and language delay with suspected hearing loss
  • Dizziness and balance disorders
  • Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV)
  • Vestibular neuronitis
  • Internuclear ophthalmoplegia (INO)
  • Balance problems after traumatic brain injury
  • Semicircular canal dehiscence
  • Meniere's disease
  • Otolith organ-related vestibular dysfunction

Breast surgery deals with the surgical treatment of breast diseases, most notably breast cancer, where early diagnosis can make a meaningful difference to treatment options. At our partner hospital, breast surgeons work alongside medical oncology, plastic surgery, radiology and pathology so that each plan reflects the individual's diagnosis and preferences. MedLuxLife helps you gather your imaging and biopsy results and arranges a multidisciplinary opinion before any decision is made.

Treatments and services

Multidisciplinary breast care

Diagnosis and treatment planning involve breast surgery, medical oncology, plastic surgery, radiology, pathology and other specialists as needed.

Lumpectomy (breast-conserving surgery)

Removal of the tumour together with a small margin of surrounding healthy tissue, preserving the rest of the breast.

Total mastectomy

Removal of the entire breast, which may be considered in early- or later-stage breast cancer depending on the individual situation.

Nipple-sparing mastectomy

Removal of breast tissue while preserving the skin and nipple, usually combined with an implant to restore breast shape.

Prophylactic mastectomy

Preventive removal of breast tissue that may be discussed with people at high risk of breast cancer to help reduce that risk.

Individual choice of technique

The surgical approach is selected according to the stage of disease, the patient's condition and their wishes.

Treatments and services

Detailed pain assessment

A structured consultation explores when, where and how the pain occurs, its intensity and its effect on work and daily life.

Symptom-based diagnostics

Diagnostic methods are selected to match each patient's symptoms in order to identify the cause of the pain.

Endometriosis evaluation

Multidisciplinary team

Women's health specialists work together with urology, gastroenterology, general surgery, physical therapy and psychiatry.

Perinatology, a division of obstetrics and gynaecology, focuses on the health of mother and baby during pregnancy. Alongside routine pregnancy care and delivery, it provides follow-up and management of high-risk pregnancies and the diagnosis and management of maternal and fetal conditions using specialised scans, tests and procedures. MedLuxLife helps expectant parents arrange screening, specialist scans and consultations at our partner hospital and coordinates every step of the visit.

Treatments and services

Routine and high-risk pregnancy care

Pregnancy follow-up and delivery, with closer monitoring and management for high-risk pregnancies.

First-trimester screening (11-14 weeks)

An ultrasound nuchal translucency measurement, which can be combined with blood tests and further markers such as the fetal nasal bone, blood flow in the fetal heart and the facial angle, to assess the risk of Down syndrome and other conditions.

Second-trimester screening (15-21 weeks)

A triple or quadruple blood test that estimates risk; a raised result indicates that diagnostic testing may be advisable, not that the baby is affected.

Early detailed anomaly scan (11-14 weeks)

A detailed transvaginal ultrasound examination of fetal development early in pregnancy.

Detailed anomaly scan (18-22 weeks)

A high-resolution second-level ultrasound examining fetal organs and growth, which can include uterine artery Doppler and cervical length assessment in at-risk pregnancies.

Fetal echocardiography

A detailed examination of the baby's heart structure and function, recommended when there is an increased risk of congenital heart disease or a suspected abnormality; ideally performed around 18-21 weeks.

Doppler ultrasound

Maternal and fetal Doppler examinations to assess blood flow to the placenta and within the baby's circulation.

Chorionic villus sampling (CVS)

A placental tissue sample, usually taken at 11-14 weeks under ultrasound guidance, to examine chromosome number and structure.

Amniocentesis

A small sample of amniotic fluid, usually taken at 16-22 weeks, for chromosomal analysis; rapid FISH testing for selected chromosomes may give preliminary results sooner.

Cordocentesis (fetal blood sampling)

A small blood sample from the umbilical cord vein, usually after the 19th week, for diagnostic testing.

Counselling and birth planning

Results are discussed with parents, and findings such as a heart abnormality help plan where and how the birth should take place.

  • 11-14 week screening tests
  • 15-21 week screening tests (triple or quadruple test)
  • 11-14 week transvaginal detailed fetal anomaly screening
  • 18-22 week obstetric detailed anomaly screening
  • Fetal echocardiography
  • Maternal and fetal Doppler ultrasonography
  • Uterine artery Doppler
  • Cervical length assessment
  • Chorionic villus sampling (CVS)
  • Amniocentesis, including FISH analysis
  • Fetal blood sampling (cordocentesis)

Coexisting conditions found during the assessment are treated before transplantation is planned.

Algology, or pain medicine, focuses on identifying the source of chronic pain and building a treatment plan around the individual, including pain whose cause is difficult to pin down. At our partner hospital, a pain specialist examines each patient in detail before recommending options, which may combine medical, interventional and lifestyle measures. MedLuxLife arranges the consultation, shares your records in advance and coordinates any follow-up.

Treatments and services

Chronic pain treatment

Assessment and personalised management of long-standing pain, with the aim of finding its underlying cause.

Interventional pain treatment

Image-guided and needle-based procedures that target the structures thought to be generating pain.

Cancer pain management

Pain control tailored to people living with cancer, coordinated with their wider treatment.

Acupuncture (dry needling)

A needle-based therapy that may be used alongside other approaches to help relieve muscular and chronic pain.

Ozone therapy

Medical ozone treatment, including autohaemotherapy, offered as part of selected pain treatment plans.

Epiduroscopy

A minimally invasive endoscopic examination of the epidural space that can be used in the assessment and treatment of certain back and leg pain.

Epidural steroid injection

Injection of medication into the epidural space, which may help reduce inflammation-related spinal and radiating pain.

Regional and sympathetic nerve blocks

Targeted injections that interrupt pain signals along specific nerves or the sympathetic nervous system, which may provide longer-term relief in suitable patients.

Radiofrequency thermocoagulation

Controlled heat delivered by radio waves to selected nerves to reduce the transmission of pain.

Interventional radiology uses imaging such as ultrasound, CT and angiography to guide minimally invasive diagnostic and therapeutic procedures. Interventional radiologists not only diagnose disease but also take an active part in its treatment, often through a small puncture rather than open surgery. MedLuxLife coordinates your assessment at our partner hospital, including pre-procedure tests, and supports you through recovery and travel home.

Image-guided biopsies

Fine-needle aspiration and Tru-cut biopsies guided by ultrasound and/or CT for the neck and thyroid, chest, abdominal organs and bones.

Diagnostic angiography

Contrast imaging of arteries, usually via the femoral artery, with high-resolution and 3D imaging to show even small vessel branches.

Venography

Imaging of veins to investigate thrombosis, tumour blockages and adrenal tumours, or to assess the saphenous vein before bypass surgery.

Chest procedures

Non-vascular interventions such as thoracentesis, abscess drainage and stenting of tracheobronchial narrowing.

Balloon and stent treatment of narrowed or blocked arteries throughout the body, from the carotid and brain vessels to the legs.

Coil embolisation of brain aneurysms, embolisation of AVMs and fistulas, and intra-arterial thrombolysis in acute stroke within a limited time window.

Embolisation for bleeding and tumours

Embolisation for nosebleeds, coughing up blood and acute gastrointestinal bleeding, and for head and neck tumours.

Aortic and peripheral endografts

Covered stents for aneurysms of the thoracic and abdominal aorta and for pseudoaneurysms in peripheral arteries.

Oncological interventions

Transarterial chemoembolisation and RF ablation for liver tumours, portal vein interventions and venous port placement.

Venous and dialysis access

Venous angioplasty and stenting, dialysis catheters, fistula angioplasty, vena cava filters, TIPS and venous catheters.

Uterine fibroid embolisation and diabetic foot

Fibroid embolisation as an alternative to surgery, and balloon and laser angioplasty for narrowed foot vessels in diabetes.

Sleeve gastrectomy reduces the size of the stomach, which limits food intake and leads to significant, sustainable weight loss. One of the most widely performed weight-loss operations today.

Hair transplantation moves healthy hair follicles from areas where hair is resistant to thinning, usually the back and sides of the head, to areas with thinning or hair loss. It is one of the most requested aesthetic procedures for men and women with pattern hair loss, and the results grow naturally with your own hair.

Hair transplantation treatments

Hair and Scalp Analysis

Before any treatment, an AI-supported digital analysis evaluates hair density and thickness, the health of individual follicles and whether they are in a growth or resting phase. This helps to choose the most suitable technique and to track your progress objectively over time.

Free consultation →

FUE (Follicular Unit Extraction)

Individual follicles are taken one by one from the donor area with a fine, circular micro-punch and implanted into the thinning areas. No linear scar, and a comfortable recovery.

Learn more →

Beard and Moustache Transplant

For a fuller, more defined beard or moustache. Follicles, usually from the back of the head, are transplanted into sparse areas. An effective option for uneven growth, scarring or hair loss caused by genetics, hormones or injury.

Learn more →

Eyebrow Transplant

Reshapes and strengthens thin, sparse or over-plucked eyebrows with your own hair follicles. A permanent, natural-looking alternative to make-up or microblading.

Learn more →

Sapphire FUE

An advanced form of FUE in which the channels are opened with blades made of sapphire crystal instead of steel. The finer, sharper blades allow very precise incisions, with less tissue trauma and swelling.

Free consultation →

DHI (Direct Hair Implantation)

Follicles are implanted directly with a special implanter pen (Choi pen), without opening channels in advance. This allows precise control of angle, direction and depth.

Learn more →

FUT (Follicular Unit Transplantation)

A strip of skin is taken from the donor area and divided into individual follicular units. FUT allows many grafts in one session but leaves a longer linear scar, so it is used today only in selected cases.

Free consultation →

Restorative Hair Therapies

Not every case of thinning hair needs surgery. Restorative hair therapies nourish and stimulate the hair follicles, help to slow hair loss and improve hair density and quality. They can be used on their own or to support the results of a hair transplant.

Exosome Therapy

Exosomes are tiny vesicles released by cells that carry proteins, lipids and growth signals. For hair restoration they are usually derived from mesenchymal stem cells and injected into thinning areas of the scalp, where they stimulate the follicles, extend the growth phase and support a healthier scalp. Exosomes are often combined with PRP.

Free consultation →

Hair Mesotherapy

A tailored blend of vitamins, amino acids, plant extracts and other active ingredients is injected into the scalp to nourish the hair follicles. Usually performed as a series of sessions; many patients notice thicker, stronger hair over time.

A motorised mesotherapy device delivers even micro-injections at a controlled depth, which makes the treatment quicker and more comfortable than manual injections.

Free consultation →

Red Light Therapy

A non-invasive, low-level light treatment at wavelengths of around 600 to 650 nanometres. The light is absorbed by the follicle cells, stimulates their energy production, improves local circulation and supports healthy hair growth.

Free consultation →

PRP (Platelet-Rich Plasma)

A small amount of your own blood is processed in a centrifuge to obtain plasma rich in platelets. Injected into the scalp, it stimulates the hair follicles and supports cell renewal. PRP is a well-established option to reduce hair loss and improve hair density.
